i.norm: Tests that HTML named entities whose names contain letters AND digits (e.g. sup1, frac14) survive a parse-and-serialise round-trip correctly, both when the output charset is ASCII (entities must be re-emitted) and when it is UTF-8 (characters can be written verbatim).
The six entities under test: superscript digits ¹²³ and vulgar fractions ¼½¾. Their names all mix letters and digits, which is the edge-case this test exercises.
The plain Unicode text that the six entities represent.

── ASCII output ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Characters outside ASCII cannot be encoded directly, so jsoup must re-emit them as named entity references in the serialised HTML.

── UTF-8 output ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── UTF-8 can represent all these characters directly, so jsoup should emit the literal Unicode string rather than entity references.
